# First ignition from outside (render study)

Owner ask 2026-11-01 18:38Z: a render of the new ship while the engine starts, the first ignition, from outside. Presentation only:
no geometry, parameter or canon change. Ship: main 90df1a9 (longitudinal tanks, 289.5 m) plus the Graded Thermal Blade
(branch claude/project-thread-qlrsa7, b320e9d, owner review pending), the newest built ship.

## Function

Show what an outside observer would actually see when the D-³He drive comes up, at the B01 operating point, without the display-only
drive layers (the plasma tubes) and without glow added for looks (HSFP).

## Fixed constraints (from the spec)

- Effective exhaust velocity 19,201 km/s (0.064 c), peak thrust 21.77 MN, peak fusion power 261 TW (operating_point.burn).
- Four magnetic nozzles N1-N4 at ±2.6 m, exit plane X -144.75 m, exit coil bore r 0.69 m (drive_manifold).
- FIRST_IGNITION: rings stopped and locked, radiators in high-power rejection; hot blades 1800 K at ε 0.90 at full power (WORKING).
- Sun, exposure and light calibration from `[look.exterior]` (look.exterior: S = E·L/(Ev·Y)); Phase 4 exterior grammar (p4_hero).
- The plume boundary and luminosity are OPEN (physics.plume_boundary); the startup ramp time is OPEN (S7, OD-009).

## Light budget (plume.py, results/plume.json)

Startup shown at 30 % of full power (6.5 MN, 0.34 kg/s, ~78 TW fusion). Full power for comparison.

| Source | Startup 30 % | Full power | vs sunlit hull (startup / full) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Beam density at the exit | 1.8e18 m⁻³ (3e-9 kg/m³) | 5.9e18 m⁻³ | — |
| Ion energy | ~1.9 MeV per nucleon | same | — |
| Beam recombination, 100 m | 0.7 W visible | 7 W | invisible |
| Beam bremsstrahlung, 100 m | 4 W (X-ray) | 49 W | invisible |
| Balmer sheath (edge burn-out of the last neutral H) | 20 kW, e-fold 3.8 m | 6.6 kW, e-fold 1.1 m | 0.06 / 0.10 (crest, more edge-on) |
| Nozzle refractory (quasi-steady) | 1554 K | 2100 K | 0.18 / 11 |
| Hot blades (quasi-steady) | 1332 K, deep red | 1800 K, orange | 0.03 / 4.0 |

Reading: the exhaust beam is close to invisible. What you see at ignition is the nozzle hardware starting to glow, the blades beginning
to glow red, and a faint pink-magenta sheath (Hα 656 nm with Hβ/Hγ) a few metres long hugging each beam's edge while neutral hydrogen is
still leaving the nozzles. Against a sunlit hull the sheath is lost; against black space and on the night side it reads.

## PROTOTYPE choices (brackets)

- Startup fraction 30 % (the WF_DRIVE_STARTUP drive_active 0.3 step); neutral fraction 1 % at startup (0.1-3 %), 0.1 % at full power.
- Neutral gas speed 3 km/s (2-5), edge density 1.5 % of the core (0.5-5 %), sheath half-width 0.3 m (0.1-0.6), beam half-angle 10°
  (inside the 5/10/15/20° study cones), S/XB 15 (10-20), ⟨σv⟩ion 3e-14 m³/s, plume Te 50 eV (10-500).
- Liner face 2100 K at full power (must sit above the 1800 K hot loop it feeds), ε 0.35; temperatures follow power^¼ (quasi-steady; the
  thermal transient is OPEN, so the startup frame may show the blades cooler still).
- Sun direction per shot is a presentation choice (attitude and pointing OPEN). The night-side shot is +3 EV, as a camera exposing
  for the shadow would be; the others are at the matched exposure.

## Unknowns

Plume boundary, neutral fraction and its time history, ramp duration, liner and blade transients, the stray light from the reactor
(X-ray and neutron, not visible). None of these moves geometry.

## Outputs

`runs/renders/first_ignition_render/first_ignition_{wide,drive,shadow,full_power}.png` and `REVIEW_FIRST_IGNITION.blend` (packed, opens
on CAM_FI_WIDE in the startup pose; WORK_IGNITION_PLUME holds the sheath volumes, sun and cameras), copied to the project folder.
